content:
The Percentages chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Percentages tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Percentages

Questions on percentage change, successive percentage change, product-constancy (price–consumption) and applications in profit-loss, data interpretation and growth.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • x% of N = (x/100)·N; A as % of B = (A/B)·100.
  • Successive changes a% then b% give a net a + b + ab/100 %.
  • A 20% rise then a 20% fall is a net 4% loss, not 0%.
  • If price rises x%, consumption must fall x/(100+x)·100 % to keep spend constant.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Adding percentages taken on different bases.
  • Assuming +x% then −x% cancels out.
  • Confusing "x% more than" with "x% less than".

quiz.title: CAT Percentages Practice Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten CAT-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: If A is 125% of B, then B is what percentage of (A + B)?
questions.explanation: Let B = 100. Since A is 125% of B, A = 125. The sum (A + B) = 125 + 100 = 225. We need to find what percentage B is of (A + B). Required percentage = (B / (A + B)) * 100 = (100 / 225) * 100 = (4 / 9) * 100 = 44.44%.

questions.q: A machine depreciates in value by 20% every year. If its value after 3 years is Rs. 51,200, find its initial purchase value.
Two numbers A and B are such that 20% of A is equal to 30% of B. If the average of A and B is 225, find the value of |A - B|.
questions.explanation: Given 0.20A = 0.30B ⇒ 2A = 3B ⇒ A/B = 3/2. Let A = 3x and B = 2x. Average of A and B is (3x + 2x)/2 = 2.5x = 225 ⇒ x = 225 / 2.5 = 90. Therefore, A = 270 and B = 180. Difference |A - B| = 270 - 180 = 90 ? Wait: 3x - 2x = x = 90. Let's check options: 90 is option D. Let's re-verify: Average is (3x+2x)/2 = 2.5x = 225 ⇒ x

questions.q: If 35% of a number is subtracted from itself, the result is equal to 52% of another number. If the second number is 250, what is the value of the first number?
questions.explanation: Let the first number be N₁ and the second number be N₂ = 250. According to the question, N₁ - 0.35N₁ = 0.52N₂ ⇒ 0.65N₁ = 0.52 × 250. 0.65N₁ = 130 ⇒ N₁ = 130 / 0.65 = 20000 / 65 = 400.

questions.q: Two numbers X and Y are such that 35% of X is equal to 55% of Y. If the sum of X and Y is 360, find the value of |X - Y|.
questions.explanation: Given 0.35X = 0.55Y ⇒ 35X = 55Y ⇒ 7X = 11Y ⇒ X/Y = 11/7. Let X = 11k and Y = 7k. Sum 11k + 7k = 18k = 360 ⇒ k = 20. Therefore, X = 220 and Y = 140. Difference |X - Y| = 220 - 140 = 80.

questions.q: A number is increased by 20% and then decreased by 20%. What is the net percentage change in the number?
questions.explanation: Let the original number be 100.,After a 20% increase: 100 + 20% of 100 = 120.,After a 20% decrease on 120: 120 - 20% of 120 = 96.,Net change = 96 - 100 = -4, which is a 4% decrease.

questions.q: A shopkeeper sells an item for ₹1200 at a loss of 20%. What should be the selling price to gain a 20% profit?
questions.explanation: Let the cost price (CP) be ₹x.,Selling at a 20% loss: 80% of CP = 1200 → 0.8x = 1200 → x = 1500.,To gain 20% profit: Selling Price = 120% of CP = 1.2 * 1500 = ₹1800.

questions.q: If 45% of a number is added to itself, the result becomes equal to 65% of another number. If the second number is 300, find the value of the first number.
questions.explanation: Let the first number be N₁ and the second number be N₂ = 300. According to the problem, N₁ + 0.45N₁ = 0.65N₂ ⇒ 1.45N₁ = 0.65 × 300. 1.45N₁ = 195 ⇒ N₁ = 195 / 1.45 = 19500 / 145 = 150.

questions.q: Two numbers P and Q are such that 40% of P is equal to 60% of Q. If the sum of P and Q is 300, find the value of |P - Q|.
questions.explanation: Given 0.40P = 0.60Q ⇒ 2P = 3Q ⇒ P/Q = 3/2. Let P = 3k and Q = 2k. Sum 3k + 2k = 5k = 300 ⇒ k = 60. Therefore, P = 180 and Q = 120. Difference |P - Q| = 180 - 120 = 60.

questions.q: If 55% of a number is added to itself, the result equals 85% of another number. If the second number is 400, find the value of the first number.
questions.explanation: Let the first number be N₁ and the second number be N₂ = 400. Given equation: N₁ + 0.55N₁ = 0.85N₂ ⇒ 1.55N₁ = 0.85 × 400. 1.55N₁ = 340 ⇒ N₁ = 340 / 1.55 = 34000 / 155 = 6800 / 31 = 219.35 ? Wait, let's recompute with clean numbers: let N₂ = 310, then 340 becomes 0.85 × 310 = 263.5. Let's adjust N₂ = 310: 1.55N₁ = 0.85

faq.q: Why is percentage so important for CAT?
faq.a: It is the base for Profit & Loss, Interest, Mixtures and a lot of Data Interpretation, so speed here pays off across the whole Quant + DILR section.

faq.q: What are the must-know fraction-to-percent values?
faq.a: 1/2=50%, 1/3=33.33%, 1/4=25%, 1/8=12.5%, 1/9=11.11%, 1/11=9.09% — memorise these for instant mental calculation.
